posts.content_md:
I see in Jeff Blyths formula that 1,1,3,3- tetramethylguanidine ( TMG ) is added to the DCG in addition to Methyl Blue. I think I understand this is added to increase speed (lower exposure). My question is, if you add Methyl Blue to standard DCG, is it still sensitive to HeNe light? And what is the difference in energy needed between the TMG and Non TMG emulsions. Also, if any work has been done with Methyl Blue without TMG, does the PH need to be adjusted? Basically, can I just add Methyl blue to standard DCG to render it sensitive to red light?

Jeff? Jean?

Thanks in advance,

John

posts.author: jean
posts.content_md:
Before Jeff discovers the availibility of TMG as electrons donor in MB-DCG, searchers in other labs made DCG sensible to HeNe radiation simply adding MB in DCG + AM

Even plexyglass (polymethyl methacrylate) can be red sensitive with MB.

But as you guess, you need a lot of energy too !

I think in my humble opinion that MBDCG + TMG is the best formula to shoot holograms in red light, at least for hobbyers as us.

You must buy this book, this is a bible for people who want explore the deep of emultion making.

[http://bookstore.spie.org/index.cfm?fus ... N=51747628](http://bookstore.spie.org/index.cfm?fuseaction=DetailVolume&productid=249955&CFID=1843568&CFTOKEN=51747628)

Take it ! It's a must !

About questions about pH adjusting, I let the talk to Jeff or Martin. 8) 

CY

posts.author: Sergio
posts.content_md:
POLAROID corp. used in the DMP polymer system material methylene blue and as electron donor, Corcat P-600 available from Bayer now.

Corcat P-600 is an amine soluble in water (polymer amine) that is much more safe and I believe will work well with DCG system.

Regarding pH control the Hydrion buffer capsules may work well controlling in the easy way the pH of DCG emulsion: 

[http://www.microessentiallab.com/buffer/buffcaps.html](http://www.microessentiallab.com/buffer/buffcaps.html)

.
